messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: P1 - KV_CACHE_PRESSURE affecting inference-serving-us-east-1. Multiple pods reporting p95/p99 spikes and streaming stalls. Incident: PD-7852. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENTS/PD-7852

pagerduty-bot: Affected services: inference-runtime, kv-cache-shard-3, streaming-proxy-us-east. Auto-cc: #eng-oncall, #eng-sre, #support.

sara: ack, I'm oncall. grabbing logs + topology. 

sara: quick summary from first look — p95 for text-generation routes jumped from ~120ms -> ~820ms. p99 from ~700ms -> ~4.2s. Streaming tail latency shows many stalls at chunk boundary.

michael: echo — seeing sharp increase in kv eviction rate on shard-3 since 02:03 UTC. Prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill ops dropped and decode ops dominate (approx 3:1 decode:prefill) so hot-path decode threads are queueing.

sara: adding metric snippets:
```
# grafana query (approx):
max_over_time(inference_latency_ms[5m]) by (route)
kv_evictions_total{shard="3"}
event_rate{operation="prefill"} / event_rate{operation="decode"}
```

divya: logs show repeated slab-resize and eviction bursts, plus intermittent OOM kills on a worker that was GCing. KV slab utilization near 95% on shard-3.

ops-bot: deploys-inference: recent deploy 2026-03-14T01:50Z rolled model-variant v2-quant to us-east; rollback window ends 03:30Z.

sara: possible hypothesis: new variant has larger long-term KV keys (longer context/prompts) causing fragmentation + more prefill pressure but prefill processing is slower on this variant -> decode dominates and starves prefill background workers. Net effect: eviction churn -> stalls.

michael: can someone run the quick queries to confirm prefill queue length and worker backlog? i'll start investigating slab allocator metrics.

divya: running quick checks now — output: prefill_queue_length: 42 -> normally ~5, decode_queue_length: 310. prefill worker lag (ms): 1200. eviction_rate_per_min: 980 (norm ~50).

sara: customer impact: some streaming customers in us-east are seeing repeated chunk re-sends and partial responses. CS impact likely medium-high for heavy streaming customers. Notifying support.

support-lead: on it, pinging top impacted customers and preparing status message. ETA for initial customer note: +15m.

divya: attempted soft-mitigation: reduce streaming concurrency on shard-3 (set route override) — command used:
```
# patch route concurrency
curl -X POST https://console.api/internal/routes/override \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","max_concurrency":8,"shard":"3"}'
```

divya: after reducing concurrency we saw p95 drop to ~420ms within 90s, p99 down to ~1.8s but prefill queue still elevated. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.

michael: next mitigation: enable emergency prefill-priority to force prefill workers to run at higher niceness on affected nodes. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/kv-worker PRELOAD_PRIORITY=high --selector=shard=3
```

michael: also started a selective rollback of model-variant v2-quant on shard-3 to v2-base for a canary subset (20% traffic).

sara: monitoring impact of both actions. if we see eviction_rate fall and prefill queue drain, we'll expand rollback.

eli: tagging monitoring and tracing: added epics to console dashboard for "kv:eviction-rate/shard-3" and a streaming-stall rate alert at 5m.

divya: note — forced prefill-priority caused CPU bump on worker nodes, one node spiked to 92% but no OOMs. Keeping an eye.

ops-bot: rollback task started: rollback-id: rb-339876-1 -> targeting 20% traffic on shard-3.

sara: initial customer-facing note (draft): "We are investigating increased latency in us-east affecting streaming responses. Engineers are mitigating; temporary rate limits may be applied. We will update within 30 mins." sending to support for vetting.

support-lead: approved. sent at 02:27 UTC.

michael: good signal — after rollback-canary + prefill-priority, prefill_queue_length down to 7, eviction_rate 120/min. p95 back to ~160ms, p99 ~760ms. streaming stalls largely cleared.

sara: great. marking incident as significant but contained. I'll continue monitoring for 30m, coordinating with eng-sre for root cause follow-up.

divya: long-term actions we should add to postmortem:
- investigate model-variant memory access patterns leading to larger KV entries
- improve prefill/decode worker autoscaling rules and backpressure handling
- add heuristic to detect prefill:decode imbalance and automatically throttle decode when prefill lag > threshold
- schedule slab-rebalance job to reduce fragmentation during rollout windows

michael: agree, and add: better rollout gating for model changes that affect kv sizes & eviction footprint.

sara: handoff: i'm handing to michael for the 03:10 UTC shift and the follow-up RCA. if anything regresses before then, @michael you have priority.

michael: taking over. noted action items + will set up a brief RCA meeting at 09:00 UTC to cover mitigation timeline and planned fixes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-7852 acknowledged by sara at 02:29 UTC. Severity remains P1 until mitigation confirmed stable.

sara: final ops note: current status — mitigations in place (concurrency cap, prefill-priority + canary rollback), customer notice posted, metrics trending toward normal. continuing to monitor. :white_check_mark:

eli: copying this thread into #postmortems under draft PD-7852/kv-fragmentation for RCA writeup.

michael: will run extended metric pull and attach graphs to the postmortem. expected next update in 20m.

support-lead: closing customer comms loop — notified top 5 affected customers, offering logs and a follow-up once RCA is ready.

sara: thanks team. handing off and setting a reminder to update incident status at +30m.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from michael, :eyes: from divya)
